title: Colorado River post-2026 operating rules

charter.in: The setting of new operating and sharing rules for the Colorado River (the post-2026 rules): the seven basin states' renegotiation, the federal government's 10-year operating framework and proposed mandatory cuts for Arizona, California and Nevada, and the Lake Powell and Lake Mead conditions that our stories tie to those rules. Covered from February 2026.
out: Western US drought, heat waves and wildfire risk in general
Climate attribution of Western water losses to fossil-fuel producers
California water outside the Colorado basin (Sacramento Valley aquifer, Central Valley farmland)
The marine heatwave off the US west coast
Global water-scarcity reports and droughts elsewhere
charter.endEvent: The Interior Department / Bureau of Reclamation issues final, binding operating guidelines (a final decision on the 10-year framework and the Lower Basin cuts), or the seven states sign a consensus deal that replaces the federal plan.

entries.title: Federal plan sets 10-year water rules for seven states

statuses.subject: Federal government (Bureau of Reclamation)
statuses.status: will issue a 10-year operating framework, revisited every two years, if the states fail to agree; final environmental impact statement and decision due this summer

entries.why: The federal government commits to imposing its own 10-year framework if the states don't agree. Conditional and not final, so a step, not the end.

entries.title: US plans big water cuts for Arizona, California, Nevada

statuses.subject: Federal plan
statuses.status: proposed mandatory cuts of up to 3 million acre-feet a year for Arizona, California and Nevada through 2036; binding guidelines expected by October 1

statuses.subject: Seven basin states
statuses.status: failed to agree on shared reductions

entries.why: Reclamation proposes mandatory Lower Basin cuts after the states' failure. Still a proposal, with binding guidelines due by 1 October, so a step, not the end.

notes: Not closed. Neither federal plan is the end event. The June story describes a framework the government 'will issue' only 'if seven basin states fail to agree'; its caveats say the plan is 'not final and can be supplanted' and that a final environmental impact statement and decision come 'this summer'. The August story is a proposal ('Proposal not final'), with 'binding guidelines expected by October 1'. On 18 August the plan is still 'contested'. No story reports the final binding guidelines or a seven-state deal, so the development is open on 16 November. Figures are []: the only number in 3 or more entries is the roughly 40 million people who depend on the river (all six state it), which is a fixed description, not a figure to track. The proposed cut appears twice: 'up to 3 million acre-feet' a year on 1 Aug, and 'about 3.7 billion cubic metres per year' on 18 Aug, which is the same cut in metric units. Lake Mead's '17 feet above its record low' appears once. The stories differ on the river's flow decline ('roughly 20% over the last century' on 28 Feb, 'about a third over a century' on 6 Jun). The 11 May story says deadlines were missed without naming them. Six stories carry the 'Colorado River' label (the brief said five); all six belong. ROLES: the 11 May entry accepts either verdict (`eitherRole`, saying why in `roleReview`, an AI session's review of 2026-11-22 not yet checked by a person).
